summary: Ruthenium (Ru) and ruthenium dioxide (RuO2) thin films were deposited using a novel zero-valent metalorganic precursor, (ethylbenzene)(1,3-butadiene)Ru(0), and molecular oxygen (O2) at a deposition temperature of 225 /C176C. The study focused on the ALD process for both Ru and RuO2 films, highlighting the use of the new precursor and its impact on film growth, resistivity, and step coverage.
evidence: Ruthenium (Ru) and ruthenium dioxide (RuO 2) thin ﬁlms were grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) by applying a sequential supply of a novel zero-valent metalorganic precursor, (ethylbenzene)(1,3butadiene)Ru(0) (EBBDRu, C 12H16Ru), and molecular oxygen (O 2) at a deposition temperature of 225 /C176C.
